paragraphs.text: DeepSeek Harness (dsh) web-fetch provider for hosts-file accelerators: keeps web_fetch working when
GitHub resolves to a local reverse proxy
# @citisen/dsh-github-accelerator
English | 中文

A DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`) bundle that keeps the
`web_fetch` tool working when GitHub is reached thr

ough a **hosts-file accelerator** —
SteamCommunity302, Watt Toolkit / Steam++, or anything else that

maps domains to
`127.0.0.1` and serves them from a local reverse proxy.
Without it, every `web_fetch` of GitHub fails with:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Why it fails

`dsh`'s built-in local fetch provider (`http`) resolves the request hostname, rejects the
whole answ

er set if any address is not public unicast, and pins a validated address into
the connection. That

is the right default for an anonymous fetcher — and it is exactly
what a hosts-file accelerator brea

ks, because `127.0.0.1 github.com` makes the host
resolve to a non-public address by construction.

There is a second wall right behind it. An accelerator that intercepts TLS signs an
on-the-fly certi

ficate with a CA it installed into the **operating system** certificate
store. Browsers and `curl` t

rust it; Node does not read that store, so even with the
address check out of the way the request di

es with
`UNABLE_TO_GET_ISSUER_CERT_LOCALLY`.
## What this plugin does

It registers one extra fetch provider, id `http-accelerated`, that makes exactly one
decision — is t
he request hostname on the configured allowlist?

- **On the allowlist** (GitHub by default): the request is sent to whatever the system
resolver retu

rns, so the accelerator's loopback endpoint is used, and the operating
system's trust anchors are ad

ded to the TLS handshake so the accelerator's
interception CA is accepted.
- **Everything else**: ha

nded to the built-in `http` provider unchanged. Public-address
validation, the redirect policy, byte

caps, timeouts and error codes stay exactly as
shipped.

Ordinary fetching therefore behaves as before. A private destination that is *not* on
the allowlist
(say `http://127.0.0.1:8080/`) is still refused by the built-in provider.
## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness with the `web` service and the built-in `http` fetch provider
(any stock profile)

. Tested on dsh `0.2.1-rc.2` (desktop, Electron 44 / Node 24.21).
- Node ≥ 24.9 in the `dsh` host fo

r the operating-system trust store
(`tls.getCACertificates`). On older runtimes the plugin falls bac

k to Node's bundled
roots, and an accelerator's own CA needs `insecureTLS: true`.
## Install

Through the Web UI: **Plugins → install**, enter `@citisen/dsh-github-accelerator`, then
enable it.

**Plugins → install**, enter `@citisen/dsh-github-accelerator`, then

`dsh plugin` forwards to pnpm inside the profile and then reconciles
`dsh.profile.bundles`; because

this package declares `dsh.bundle`, enabling it needs no
hand-edited YAML.

Use `--profile web` instead of `--profile desktop` if you run the browser profile from
the CLI. `dsh

` hot-reloads the profile, but fully quit and reopen the application if the

reloads the profile, but fully quit and reopen the application if the

### From a local checkout
[代码示例省略，未执行]

then add `"@citisen/dsh-github-accelerator"` to `dsh.profile.bundles` in that profile's
`package.jso

n`. On Windows a link across drives is unreliable in pnpm: it can resolve to
a non-existent path, af

ter which the bundle reconciliation silently skips the package.
Fix the link by hand (`rmdir node_mo

dules\@citisen\dsh-github-accelerator`, then
`mklink /J` the real directory) and add the bundle entr

sen\dsh-github-accelerator`, then
`mklink /J` the real directory) and add the bundle entry yourself.
## Configure

The bundle ships a working default (GitHub's own hosts). To change it, override the row
in your prof
ile's `cordis.patch.yml` — your layer wins over the bundle layer:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
| Key | Default | Meaning |
| `hosts` | GitHub hosts | Hostnames allowed to resolve to non-public addresses. `*.example.com` mat

ches `example.com` and every subdomain; `*` matches everything (not recommended) |
| `trustSystemCer
tificates` | `true` | Add the OS certificate store to the TLS trust anchors for allowlisted hosts. T

his is what accepts a local accelerator's CA |
| `insecureTLS` | `false` | Skip certificate verifica

tion for allowlisted hosts. Last resort only, for a CA that cannot be installed in the store |
| `ti

meoutMs` | `30000` | Deadline for one fetch, including the body read |
| `maxResponseBytes` | `50000

00` | Body byte cap; a declared oversize body fails with `WEB_FETCH_TOO_LARGE` |
| `maxBodyChars` |

`100000` | Decoded character cap; longer bodies are truncated and flagged |
| `maxRedirects` | `5` |

Same-origin redirect hops |
| `userAgent` | dsh's default UA | Request header |
[该节后续省略]
## Security notes

- Allowlisted hosts no longer get the "must be public" check. That is the point of the
plugin, and i

t is the cost: if an allowlisted name is pointed at an internal service,
`web_fetch` will reach it.

Keep the list small.
- TLS for allowlisted hosts trusts everything the operating system trusts. That

matches
browser behaviour, and is broader than Node's bundled roots.
- Everything off the allowlist

is still handled by the built-in provider, unchanged.
- Only the model-facing `web_fetch` path is a

ffected. `git`, `curl` and package managers
in the shell use their own configuration and were never
blocked by this error.
## How it works

`cordis.patch.yml` pins the `web` service to `http-accelerated` and inserts one row. The
plugin's `a
pply` registers a `WebFetchProvider` that:

1. parses the URL and matches the hostname against `hosts`;
2. on a match, performs the request with

`node:https`/`node:http` against the system
resolver's answer, following same-origin redirects and
therwise calls the provider registered under `http` and returns its result verbatim.

The provider is a plain ESM module with no `@deepseek-ai/*` imports, so it can be loaded
and tested

s a plain ESM module with no `@deepseek-ai/*` imports, so it can be loaded
and tested outside `dsh`.
